newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: N.Ireland Loyalists threaten to attack Ireland.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Loyalists threaten to attack Ireland.

text.p: A maverick Northern Ireland Loyalist group claimed responsibility on Monday for an abortive bomb attack on the border town of Dundalk and threatened further no-warning attacks against Ireland.
The Loyalist Volunteer Force (LVF), a breakaway group of extremists fighting to maintain British rule of Northern Ireland, made the claim in a call to a Northern Ireland television station.
The LVF, which was formed in the past six months, said in the statement that Sunday's bomb had failed to detonate "because of technical difficulties which have now been sorted".
It was referring to a device left in an alley in Dundalk, on the Irish border with the British province, which failed to detonate properly. It was destroyed in a controlled army explosion.
"Further attacks will continue so long as Dublin interferes in Ulster's affairs," the statement said. "These attacks will take the form of no-warning bomb attacks as in Dundalk."
